Fix three problems with print-host printers (Klipper/Moonraker, OctoPrint, PrusaLink and the like) on JusPrin's Home page and header. Reproduce each one on the real built app before fixing it, and show it working afterwards.

1. **A printer that never answers shows as connected.** A print-host printer whose address answers nothing still gets "Connected · <address>" and a green "Idle" dot on its Home card, and the "Open printer window" button. JusPrin checks only Moonraker hosts. Every other host type counts as connected once an address is saved. See `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` around lines 335-365 (`can_launch_monitor`, `connection_state`, `Printers::host_status`).
2. **Its window stays blank.** Clicking "Open printer window" for that printer opens a plain white window. It stayed blank for over two minutes with no message. The window is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/PrinterWindow.cpp`. It holds Orca's `PrinterWebView`, whose `OnError` only logs. The person should see in plain words that the printer's page didn't load and what to do. Fix this in JusPrin's own files, not by editing `PrinterWebView.cpp`, unless you justify that under `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`.
3. **The header menu can't open the window.** When the project's printer is a print-host printer, the first row of the header's printer menu reads "Not connected · Prints go to a card." and is greyed out, with no way to open the printer's window. Home calls the same printer "Idle". The cause is that `SetupCommands::printer_connection()` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SetupCommands.cpp`, about lines 272-295) reports state only for Bambu printers. The menu row is built in `PrinterMenu::show_root` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp`). The row should open the same window the Home card opens, through `OrcaHomeBackend::open_printer_window`.

- Open windows are tracked by printer name (`m_printer_windows`), so after a rename the old window keeps its title, and a click opens a second window for the same printer.
- After the printer's address changes, a click brings back the old window still showing the old address.

# Home printer card monitor button: investigation notes (2026-11-04)

Investigation only; nothing in the repo was edited. Build: build/arm64 RelWithDebInfo at e27c962864, run from a scratch copy with its own --datadir.

## What the spec says
- product-definition.md section 3.4: Monitor is a pop-out surface that stays visible while the person works elsewhere. It owns camera, progress/layer/time left, printer state, temperatures, health and fault alerts, and Pause/Resume/Stop. Home "launches Monitor" (section 3.1).
- Canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, comp-printer-card: only the expanded card of a printing Bambu X1 Carbon has "Launch monitor"; the collapsed idle card has none. main-02-printer-popover-overlay draws a monitor glyph on every printer row, the offline Voron included.
- No board draws the Monitor screen itself. Nothing says what a print host (Moonraker, OctoPrint) should open, or whether an offline or faulted printer gets the button.

## How it was reproduced without screen control
Screen control was denied twice. What worked:
- JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL pointed at a copy of resources/jusprin/home/index.html with an injected script. The script logs envelopes to a local server and clicks or posts the messages it is given from a queue folder.
- Kenneth's JusPrin2 data was copied to a scratch folder. In the copy, `recent`/`recent_projects` were emptied: startup hung in FileHistory::LoadThumbnails otherwise. local_machines was emptied, and the copy got fake_printer=true plus jusprin_printer_devices {FAKE001: "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2"} and jusprin_verified_connections {FAKE001: true}. A user preset "Klipper Pi" was added, inheriting "MyKlipper 0.4 nozzle", with host_type moonraker and print_host http://raspberrypi.local.
- `lldb -p <pid> --batch -o "expr -l c++ -- ((Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxAppConsoleBase::ms_appInstance)->mainframe->m_tabpanel->GetSelection()"` reads which main-window page is showing. SetSelection(0) or (1) moves between Home and Prepare.
- The MCP `printer_setup {printerPreset}` call changed the project's printer at runtime.

## Results
1. Bambu card, Bambu preset selected: the main window switches from Home to Orca's Device page (page 3 = MonitorPanel, shown on screen; the 3D view is hidden; the project header stays on top). This is not a pop-out.
2. Klipper card: a separate 1200x800 window opens on Orca's PrinterWebView with the host's own page (Mainsail). The card said "Connected · raspberrypi.local" and offered the button while Klipper reported shutdown, because Moonraker itself answers.
3. Bambu card, Klipper preset selected for the project: "Launch monitor" switches the main window to page 3, which now holds the Klipper printer's web page (m_printer_view shown, m_monitor hidden). The Bambu printer's monitor never appears, and the hidden MonitorPanel switches the device manager's selected machine from raspberrypi.local to FAKE001.
4. Fake caveat: launching the monitor for the already-selected LAN machine makes upstream disconnect and reconnect it (DevManager.cpp:519-530). The fake answers that disconnect with "lost", and GUI_App.cpp:2112 then selects no machine, so the monitor ends up showing no printer. Whether Bambu's real plug-in does the same is unverified.

## Side observation, not monitor scope
With the Klipper preset selected, the agent switches to "orca" and Home gains a second card, "raspberrypi.local · Not connected" (id device:raspberrypi.local), beside "Klipper Pi · Connected".

## Fix implemented (uncommitted), after Kenneth chose "Own window per printer"
- New Home/PopOutWindow (shared base: icon, sizing, deferred safe destroy, moved out of PrinterWindow), Home/MonitorWindow (a second Orca MonitorPanel in its own frame, sized to the panel's best size within the screen, titled with the printer's name).
- OrcaHomeBackend::launch_monitor and the header printer menu's monitor row both call OrcaHomeBackend::open_monitor_window(device). SetupCommands::open_monitor (which selected the Notebook tab) is replaced by monitored_device().
- Verified on the scratch app: card click opens one window, main window stays on Home, second click reuses it, Klipper window still opens, three close/reopen races leave one window, quitting via the main window with both pop-outs open exits 0.
- In-process window render: lldb `cacheDisplayInRect:toBitmapImageRep:` on the NSWindow's contentView writes a PNG without screen-recording permission (run/snap.sh).
- Traps: closing a window *inside* an lldb expression trips lldb's C++-exception stop and leaves a half-closed window; schedule closes with performSelector:afterDelay: instead. Quitting via [NSApp terminate:] aborts in the Bambu plug-in's static std::thread; close the main window instead.
